S1: when preparing replacement, requires arbitrary validated integers and positive denominator; ensures explicit expected results covering existing vectors, zero, negative values, even/odd half ties, large integers, and values immediately around large half ties; verify deterministic integer quotient/remainder expectations. S2: when replacing division, requires S1; ensures exact integer-to-Decimal conversion, isolated local context, explicitly sufficient precision, ROUND_HALF_EVEN, int output, and unchanged caller context; verify regression assertions and low ambient-precision scenarios. Precision must scale with operands; default Decimal precision is insufficient. S3: when implementation is complete, requires S2; ensures all acceptance assertions pass; verify python3 -B test_rounding.py. These tests establish covered numeric behavior, not exhaustive correctness; precision sufficiency also requires mathematical justification.

findings.reason: Integer division converts to float before rounding, losing precision for large integers. For example, (2**53 + 1, 1) should return 9007199254740993 but float conversion cannot preserve that integer. This is a static finding; runtime verification was blocked.
The existing three small half-tie assertions do not cover zero, large integers, or values around rounding thresholds, so they cannot establish the requested accuracy improvement.
